headline: Ukraine says it is about to start using an AI model, built with NATO, that forecasts where and when Russian drone strikes will land.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a new military AI tool announced by a government and built with NATO, but its accuracy rests on the ministry's own statement.
importance_line: Ukrainian troops and civilians under drone attack could get earlier warning, and NATO, whose new analysis centre was set up to turn lessons from the war into tools, gains a test of the approach, but the high probability claim comes from Ukraine's ministry, no track record is given, and NATO's bodies had not replied to Business Insider.
summary: Business Insider reports that Ukraine's defense ministry said on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that its forces are about to start using "Model 13", an AI model developed with NATO's Allied Command Transformation, which analyses past combat data, weather and battlefield conditions to forecast with "high probability" the time, place, intensity and type of Russian drone strikes. The ministry says the model has been validated on real-world data and is ready to be added to the army's situational awareness systems, while a second joint model, Model 32, which plans artillery deployments, is still a prototype in testing.
notes: Full Business Insider text read from the pre-fetched file. Official name is 'Model No. 13' (and No. 32); written 'Model 13' and 'Model 32' in the summary. A forecasting model, not a machine acting, so machine_action is false.
